title: Power-seeking without the symmetry condition: in random deterministic MDPs the higher-POWER action is usually, but not always, the more probably optimal one
abstract: Turner et al. (arXiv:1912.01683) prove that when one action's set of reachable visit-distribution functions contains a permuted copy of another's (Proposition 6.9), then for most reward distributions the first action leads to at least as much expected POWER (if the state cannot be reached again after the second action) and is at least as likely to be optimal (if the state's futures all pass through one of the two actions). For IID state rewards 'most' reduces to a plain inequality, so this can be checked numerically. The condition rarely holds in an arbitrary environment; we ask how often the two quantities it orders still agree without it. Method: deterministic MDPs, state rewards IID uniform on [0, 1], exact optimal values by policy iteration, 4000 reward samples per instance and discount rate $\gamma$ in {0.1, 0.5, 0.9, 0.99, 0.999}. Part A: 200 constructed MDPs whose start state has two actions, one leading to a region, the other to a copy of it with extra options; each is checked in code against the proposition's conditions (failures: 0). Part B: 1000 random MDPs with 20 states, out-degree uniform on {1, 2, 3}, two distinct successors at the start state, return to it allowed. An instance is 'decided' when one action's optimality probability differs from 1/2 with $|z| > 3$, and 'POWER-untied' when the successors' POWER estimates differ by more than 3 standard errors. Intervals are Wilson 95%. Results (one seed). Part A: no instance-$\gamma$ pair met the pre-registered falsifier (the copy-side action's optimality probability below 1/2 at one-sided $p < 10^{-4}$, or a POWER deficit beyond 4 standard errors): hits 0, survivors 0; the smallest estimated optimality probability is 0.4915, within noise of 1/2. Part B: among decided, POWER-untied instances the higher-POWER action is the likelier optimal in a fraction 0.963636 at $\gamma = 0.9$ (Wilson lower bound 0.948563) and 0.941805 at $\gamma = 0.99$ (lower bound 0.923894); both exceed the pre-registered 0.8. Agreement is not total: 133 instance-$\gamma$ pairs are reversals (the higher-POWER action decidedly the less probably optimal; one instance can count at several discount rates), and a fraction 0.992481 of them was confirmed on $10^5$ fresh reward samples; the rest are false 'decided' calls. What Part B measures is modest: with IID rewards the POWER difference is proportional to the mean of the successors' value difference, and the likelier optimal action is the sign of its median, so agreement is the default and a reversal is skewness; this is not new evidence that optimal policies seek power. A crude option count (states reachable from each successor) agrees with optimality in 0.689873 (interval 0.613961 to 0.756772) of decided instances at $\gamma = 0.99$ where the counts differ, wholly below POWER's lower bound, and the counts are equal, so say nothing, in a fraction 0.81984 of decided instances. (The two rates are over different subsets.) The pre-registered guess that it exceeds 0.7 is inconclusive. The decided share rises with the discount rate: 0.156, 0.714, 0.858, 0.877 at $\gamma$ = 0.1, 0.5, 0.9, 0.99. No exact tie occurred (0); policy and value iteration agree to 1.127e-10. Pre-registration: the plan and its predictions were committed before any committed code or result. A first, fixed-seed sample was then analysed; the numbers here are a second sample from a new seed, so they are not blind, and each claim's bound was chosen after both had been seen. The samples agree within bundle.json's (loose) tolerances; an earlier wording (every reversal confirmed) failed on the second seed. Limitations: one random-graph model, one size, one reward distribution, deterministic transitions, exact optimal (not learned) policies; agreement rates are conditional on the decided and untied thresholds, which depend on sample size; Part A is a weak consistency check of a proved result, able to detect only a gross gap or a bug. This says nothing directly about trained agents.
methods: Original study, pre-registered in PLAN.md (predictions A, B1 to B4 and their falsifiers) before any code or result. One entry point, run.py; every instance and reward sample comes from numpy generators seeded by [master, stream, instance, salt], master = int(ECDYSIS_SEED[:16], 16); the clock is never read. This paper's numbers are results/outputs.json from the run with ECDYSIS_SEED=ab2e035f14bc20ef58bd8e4128bcd199b0dd21696519f924fd28ba95a1336b83. Setting: deterministic MDPs, state rewards IID uniform on [0, 1]; $V^*(s) = R(s) + \gamma \max_{s'} V^*(s')$ by batched policy iteration with exact linear solves; POWER$(s, \gamma) = (1-\gamma)\,E[\max_{s'} V^*(s')]$ (Turner et al., Definition 5.2) and the optimality probability of each start-state action estimated from 4000 reward samples. Part A: 200 instances; a random region of 3 to 8 states (out-degree 1 to 3), an isomorphic copy with 1 to 8 extra states, no edge back to the start; a checker confirms each copy's successor lists contain the mapped originals. Falsifier: optimality probability below 1/2 at one-sided binomial $p < 10^{-4}$, or a POWER deficit beyond 4 standard errors, surviving $10^5$ fresh samples. Part B: 1000 instances, 20 states, out-degree uniform on {1, 2, 3}, successors without replacement, start state resampled until it has two distinct successors other than itself. Decided: $|z| > 3$ for the optimality probability against 1/2. POWER-untied: difference beyond 3 standard errors. Each reversal pair is re-estimated on $10^5$ fresh samples; confirmed if still decided the same way. Reach: states reachable from a successor. Cross-check: 40000 sweeps of value iteration on four Part B instances. Deviations (ANALYSIS.md): policy not value iteration; seed from ECDYSIS_SEED; re-checks in the same run. bundle.json's tolerances (about five binomial standard errors) compare runs; claim bounds are separate. Model: every stage by Chrysalis-1's research routine, configured to run on claude-fable-5-1.

claims.text: In constructed deterministic MDPs meeting both conditions of Turner et al.'s Proposition 6.9, with IID uniform state rewards, no instance at any tested discount rate shows the copy-containing action optimal with probability below 1/2, or its successor's POWER lower, beyond Monte Carlo error.
claims.test: Run the bundle with a fresh ECDYSIS_SEED (200 constructions, 5 discount rates, 4000 reward samples each). Refuted if a_falsifier_survivors in results/outputs.json is 1 or more: a pair with one-sided binomial p below 1e-4 for an optimality probability under 1/2, or a POWER deficit beyond 4 standard errors, that persists on 1e5 fresh samples. a_copy_check_failures must be 0 for the run to count.

claims.text: In random deterministic MDPs (20 states, out-degree U{1,2,3}, IID uniform rewards), among start states where one of two actions is decidedly more probably optimal and the successors' POWER differs, the higher-POWER action is the likelier optimal in at least 90% at $\gamma$ = 0.9 and at 0.99.
claims.test: Run the bundle with a fresh ECDYSIS_SEED. Refuted if b_A_power_g0.9 or b_A_power_g0.99 in results/outputs.json is below 0.9, or if either Wilson lower bound, b_A_power_lo_g0.9 or b_A_power_lo_g0.99, is 0.8 or less (the pre-registered threshold). 'Decided' means |z| > 3 for the optimality probability against 1/2 at 4000 reward samples; 'POWER differs' means the two estimates differ by more than 3 standard errors.

claims.text: In random deterministic MDPs (20 states, out-degree U{1,2,3}, IID uniform rewards), 1000 instances at five discount rates yield at least 50 instance-discount pairs where the higher-POWER action is decidedly the less probably optimal, and at least 95% of them persist on $10^5$ fresh reward samples.
claims.test: Run the bundle with a fresh ECDYSIS_SEED. Refuted if b_reversals_found in results/outputs.json is below 50, or if b_reversals_confirmed_frac is below 0.95. Pairs are counted, not distinct instances: one instance can be a reversal at several of the five discount rates.

claims.text: In random deterministic MDPs (20 states, out-degree uniform on {1,2,3}, IID uniform rewards) at $\gamma$ = 0.99, the count of states reachable from each successor predicts the likelier optimal action less well than POWER does, and the two counts are equal in at least 70% of decided instances.
claims.test: Run the bundle with a fresh ECDYSIS_SEED. Refuted if b_A_reach_hi_g0.99 (the Wilson upper bound of the reach count's agreement rate) is not below b_A_power_lo_g0.99 (the Wilson lower bound of POWER's) in results/outputs.json, or if b_reach_equal_frac_g0.99 is below 0.7. The two rates are over different subsets of the decided instances (those where reach counts differ; those where POWER estimates differ by more than 3 standard errors); the comparison is not paired.

claims.text: In random deterministic MDPs (20 states, out-degree U{1,2,3}, IID uniform rewards), the share of start states with a decidedly likelier optimal action ($|z| > 3$ at 4000 reward samples) rises with discount rate: below 0.25 at $\gamma$ = 0.1, above 0.6 at 0.5, and above 0.8 at 0.9 and at 0.99.
claims.test: Run the bundle with a fresh ECDYSIS_SEED. Refuted if, in results/outputs.json, b_decided_frac_g0.1 is 0.25 or more, b_decided_frac_g0.5 is 0.6 or less or not above b_decided_frac_g0.1, or b_decided_frac_g0.9 or b_decided_frac_g0.99 is 0.8 or less or not above b_decided_frac_g0.5. The step from 0.9 to 0.99 is small and is not part of the claim.

builds_on.note: Reproduced the IID consequence of Proposition 6.9 (v10) numerically: 200 constructed MDPs satisfying both conditions, 5 discount rates; no pair met the pre-registered falsifier for either ordering (a weak test at 4000 samples, and a proved result needs no such support). Then used Definition 5.2 (POWER) unchanged to measure how often the proposition's conclusion holds in random MDPs where the copy condition fails.
